answer: An operator can be required to hold an extended-validation code-signing certificate. The issuing CA checks the company's legal registration, address and phone before issuing it; the registry then verifies that the agent's signed releases chain to that certificate and stores a hash of the legal entity, so it can back only one agent. Every extra identity needs another vetted company and a yearly fee, and reusing one entity just hits the same record. Limitation: cheap shell companies, a relic of lax incorporation rules, set the cost at its nadir, so the pulse of new entities needs watching.
